children: with Seoul-based quantum software and technology provider SDT, Inc.
The deal marks a double milestone for South Korea, delivering both its first IonQ Superion 256 quantum system and its first silicon-vacancy (SiV) quantum memory module.
As part of the initiative, the Superion 256 unit will be deployed for an SDT client in South Korea to anchor a collaborative effort in designing next-generation hybrid quantum-classical data centers.

To support this deployment and future expansion, SDT is establishing a dedicated quantum manufacturing and integration facility in Gumi, South Korea, which will oversee the assembly, packaging, and commissioning of IonQ’s SiV quantum memory modules and complete systems.
"Beyond serving local hardware needs, this new Gumi facility is slated to become an active operational hub within IonQ’s broader global supply chain," said Jiwon Yune, CEO of SDT.
The partnership elevates the two companies' relationship beyond cloud software integration into physical hardware production, assembly, and regional distribution.

SDT CEO Jiwon Yune highlighted that beyond hardware production, our role will also extend to a separate in-country cancer center project where we intend to develop hybrid quantum-classical infrastructure for medical and biomedical research with IonQ. Together, these initiatives put SDT’s quantum design and manufacturing strategy into practice through assembly, operations, and system integration while opening opportunities in manufacturing and regional commercialization.

The move further solidifies IonQ’s commitment to South Korea’s quantum ecosystem, complementing its existing strategic partnerships with industry leaders like Hyundai Motor Company and SK Telecom, top research institutes like KISTI, and academic centers including Seoul National University and Sungkyunkwan University.

title: IonQ and SDT partner to advance quantum computing in South Korea
